sections.title: Scoreboard figures and privacy
sections.what: Seeds three model-call records, then checks the trust figures show one of two checked answers passed, that freshness is empty, that product and learning have honest empty messages, that business shows no revenue, and that cost per read is calculated from the priced reads. Also checks the model call table has no column that could hold prompt or output text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the admin view must be accurate, honest about missing data, and must not store the text of prompts or answers.
sections.watch_out: The wording of empty-state messages is checked exactly, so rewording them breaks this test.

summary: Tests the admin scoreboards, which summarise trust, product, learning and business figures from recorded model calls.
purpose: Checks the scoreboard numbers are calculated correctly and that empty states are described honestly.
why: Likely reason: admins make decisions from these figures, so they must be accurate and must not hide missing data.
how: Seeds three model-call records, one passed, one fallback and one unchecked. Then checks the verifier pass rate, the empty freshness list, the empty read and calibration states, the revenue message, and the cost per read. Finally checks the call log table has no prompt or output text columns.
inputs: Three seeded model-call records and the database's table definition.
outputs: Scoreboard values such as pass rate and cost per read, with messages where there is no data.
risks: The privacy check depends on column names matching a pattern. Message wording is fixed in the test.
debug: Compare the seeded records with the expected pass count. Check the column list for the call log table if the privacy check fails.
